comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
ROOT-CAUSED VIA /rebar-debug. Full protocol, isolated worktree, three hypotheses tested at runtime. THE HEADLINE: two of the three mechanisms are INTENDED BEHAVIOUR and I did not touch them.

H1 — the bound firing: INTENDED, not a defect. Ran _validate_recovery_inputs directly: raises at 24,001; does NOT raise at exactly 24,000; raises for c97f's real 25,516 carrying diagnostic {'context_chars': 25516, 'context_char_limit': 24000}. Legitimacy rests on the module docstring ('Reject hostile/unbounded recovery work before the first recovery call'), docs/llm-framework.md:487-508 documenting the exact numbers, and tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_token_recovery.py::test_unbounded_ticket_context_fails_before_any_recovery_call which asserts len(runner.requests) == 1 — ZERO billable recovery calls on a breach. Raising or bypassing the bound would have regressed a deliberate cost safeguard. completion_recovery.py is CONFIRMED UNTOUCHED by this change.

H2 — the apparent flakiness: INTENDED, and this was the decisive experiment. With the SAME oversized 25,516-char context, a non-truncating primary returns normally and _validate_recovery_inputs is called ZERO times; with a truncating primary the abort is deterministic and the runner is called exactly once. So entry into recovery is variable (it depends on whether the live primary call hits finish_reason=length), while failure once entered is deterministic. That fully explains 'same command, different outcome' without any nondeterminism in the bound itself.

H3 — the misleading message: THE DEFECT. Confirmed at runtime that outcome_of(CompletionRecoveryError(...)) is None and hasattr(exc,'outcome') is False — .outcome is attached only at runner.py:194 and :494, and this error is raised inside completion_recovery.py, so it never passes those seams. It therefore fell through the single catch-all in transition_close.py to the generic 'install the agents extra' text, while .diagnostic (which already holds the numbers) was discarded.

FIX + THE TRAP I CAUGHT IN IT. The first version of the fix read the diagnostic keys unconditionally, so a recovery error from a DIFFERENT stage rendered 'The ticket's context (None chars) exceeds the bounded completion-recovery limit (None chars)' for an exhaustion at criterion 7 — nonsense AND a false diagnosis, i.e. the same misattribution class simply relocated. I pinned that RED first, then made the size claim conditional on the bound keys actually being present.
TESTS (4, held out from the fixer): the bound case reports size+limit and asserts no missing-extra; a NEGATIVE CONTROL that a genuine unavailability STILL gets the install-the-extra guidance (so narrowing cannot decay into deleting); the non-bound recovery case must not claim a size breach; and a collateral invariant that a bound breach never exits 11 (docs/exit-codes.md reserves 11 for retryable — an agent auto-retrying a fixed bound would loop).
MUTATION-CHECKED: re-introducing the exact root cause (neutralising the isinstance branch) returns the test to RED; restored, 4/4 green.
REGRESSIONS: the protected contract test (12 passed) and the close-gate failure matrix (35 passed) both pass; ruff + mypy clean; no new dependency; no pre-existing test modified; sibling sweep found NO other site emitting that remedy. Three unit-tier errors (build-provenance / engine-dir wheel tests, 'leaked entries into REPO_ROOT') were proven ENVIRONMENTAL by running them with my change stashed — identical failures on pristine source; they are an artifact of my PYTHONPATH harness in a venv-less worktree, not of this fix.

SCOPE HONESTY: this makes the failure ACCURATE, not absent. An oversized ticket still cannot use bounded recovery — by design. Adding a plan-review-style escalation ladder (batch → one-at-a-time → larger window → typed 'reduce the ticket' finding, per plan_review/orchestrator.py:6-15 and det_floor.py:619-656) would be a genuine DESIGN CHANGE, so it is deliberately NOT in this fix; the remaining ACs on this ticket about reconciling the bounds are left open for that decision.
Pushed as change 1027.

comments.body:
STATUS FOR HANDOFF — the messaging fix LANDED (change 1027, MERGED); the ticket is NOT fully done and should stay open.

DONE (shipped in 1027):
 * A bounded-recovery failure no longer inherits the false 'install the agents extra / set a model API key' remedy. It now reports the measured size against the limit and points at the gate_error_v1 sidecar.
 * The size claim is conditional on the bound keys being present, so a recovery failure from another stage (e.g. exhaustion at criterion 7) does not get a fabricated 'context (None chars) exceeds the limit (None chars)'.
 * A genuine unavailability STILL gets the install-the-extra guidance — pinned by a negative control so narrowing this cannot decay into deleting it.
 * returncode stays 1, not 11: the bounds re-apply on every attempt, so advertising it as retryable would loop an auto-retrying agent.
 * Tests: tests/unit/test_close_gate_bound_message_d59e.py (4), mutation-verified.

NOT DONE — deliberately, and this is the remaining scope:
 * AC 'a ticket whose description alone exceeds _MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS can still complete a close without --force-close' is met only via its OR branch (the failure now explains precisely what to shorten). An oversized ticket still cannot USE bounded recovery.
 * AC 'the interaction between _MAX_TOTAL_CRITERIA_CHARS (32,000) and _MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS (24,000) is documented or reconciled' is untouched.
WHY NOT: /rebar-debug classified the bound itself as INTENDED BEHAVIOUR, not a defect — it is a documented fail-closed cost safeguard (docs/llm-framework.md:487-508) pinned by a contract test asserting ZERO billable recovery calls on a breach. Making an oversized ticket recoverable means adding an escalation ladder (the plan-review path's sanctioned shape: batch criteria -> one-at-a-time -> larger model window -> a typed 'reduce the ticket' finding; see plan_review/orchestrator.py:6-15 and det_floor.py:619-656). That is a DESIGN CHANGE, not a bug fix, so it was left for a human decision rather than smuggled in under a bug ticket.
PRACTICAL NOTE for whoever picks this up: the failure is entered only when the PRIMARY verifier truncates, which is a property of the live call — so retrying a blocked close often succeeds. That is how c97f was eventually closed. It is a workaround, not a fix.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
(The immediately preceding one-word "PLACEHOLDER" comment was an error of mine — an unset heredoc
path. Ignore it; the store is append-only so it cannot be removed. This is the intended content.)

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW OF THE PROPOSED DESIGN — 3 load-bearing pieces INVALIDATED. Change 1060 must NOT
be submitted as-is. Every finding below was re-verified by executing the code, not taken on the
reviewer's word.

F1 [CRITICAL — signed false PASS]. The compaction committed in 1060 DELETES WHOLE CHILD TICKETS on
an epic close and mislabels it as comment elision. Mechanism: an epic verifies with graph=True
(completion.py:352-353), so assemble_context concatenates one _format_ticket block PER TICKET, each
with its own "#### Comments" heading. _split_comment_block finds the FIRST such heading and treats
everything after it as droppable comment history — which is every child's header, description and
acceptance criteria. explicit_completion_criteria only parses the ROOT description, so child
criteria are never in the protected set. Reproduced directly:
    criteria the verifier will check: ['ROOT-AC1']
    CHILD-AC survived? False | child header survived? False
    marker emitted: "[... 7 earlier comment(s) elided ... they were NOT reviewed ...]"
A child whose AC is explicitly NOT done vanishes, the verifier checks only the root criteria, and
the gate can SIGN a PASS over unfinished work while telling the operator only that "comments" were
removed. This is the worst failure class this gate has.

F2 [HIGH]. The "whole comment entry" guarantee is false: _group_comment_entries starts a new entry
on any line beginning "- ", so markdown bullets INSIDE a comment body split it. A 2-comment ticket
grouped into 4 units; compaction can drop "AC-4 deliberately deferred" while keeping "AC-1..3
done", and the elided-count in the marker is wrong too.

F4 [HIGH — my safety rationale was BACKWARDS]. I argued request_limit = genuine-large-job (recover)
vs tool_calls_limit = stuck-loop (do not recover). But runner.py:414-417 sets
request_limit = ceil(max_iter/2) and tool_calls_limit = max(8, max_iter) — verified as 240 vs 480
at the default. A classic runaway (one tool call per model turn) therefore trips request_limit
FIRST and never reaches tool_calls_limit, so the discriminant admits exactly the case it was meant
to exclude. The step-budget signal does NOT reliably separate a runaway from a big job.

F7 [MEDIUM]. Units error: sizing.container_budget returns TOKENS (868,000 for a 1M window) and the
plan used it as a CHARACTER budget. Also sizing.largest_window_tokens returns 1,000,000 for haiku,
sonnet, opus AND an unknown model alike, so the AC "changing the configured model changes the
derived budget" is unsatisfiable via that API.

F9 [HIGH — the next false-block]. _EVIDENCE_CHARS = 12,000 per criterion vs
_MAX_TOTAL_EVIDENCE_CHARS = 96,000 aggregate is incoherent above 8 criteria (96,000/14 = 6,857 mean
for 9fd4) — the SAME bound-vs-bound incoherence this ticket condemns for criteria-vs-context. Worse,
the aggregate check runs INSIDE the loop AFTER each billable call, so a 14-criterion ticket pays for
all 14 evidence calls and then hard-fails with no verdict.

F10 [HIGH]. per_criterion_steps was never stated, and the plan's own figure (~34/criterion) yields
max(480, 14 x 34) is approximately 480 — the budget that already failed. The AC "9fd4 closes at
DEFAULT settings" is not supported by the plan's own arithmetic; roughly 70-100 steps per criterion
is needed for real headroom (9fd4 spent ~780s over 240 model requests, about 3.25s each).

F11. No wall-clock deadline exists anywhere (DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S is per-request only; no SIGALRM or
deadline in the LLM path), so step scaling is NOT neutered by a timeout — but a 30-criterion ticket
at 70 steps/criterion implies roughly 57 minutes of a blocking close with no progress output.

CONSEQUENCE — the design changes. Compaction is subtle, dangerous, and (once the budget is raised)
nearly worthless. The safer design is to DROP compaction entirely: raise the budget so real tickets
fit (9fd4 is 34,282 chars; db1c's 2932 is 41,595 — a 400,000-char budget covers ~10x the worst
observed), and above it refuse with an accurate, actionable message. A refusal is a VISIBLE
false-block; a bad elision is an INVISIBLE signed false PASS, and for a signing gate that trade is
clear. Likewise F4 means the entry predicate should stop trying to classify the failure and instead
rely on recovery's own BOUNDED blast radius (per-criterion calls capped at 40 iterations),
excluding only LLMUnavailableError (the model cannot run at all) and CompletionRecoveryError (do
not nest recovery inside its own handler). F9's evidence bounds must come into scope or 9fd4 still
will not close.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
ALL 7 ACs MET — evidence, ready to close.

Landed as Gerrit change 1064 (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1, MERGED). The superseded compaction
revision 1060 is ABANDONED in Gerrit so it cannot be submitted.

AC-by-AC:
 1. Both blocked tickets reach a verdict: the cap is 100,000 chars, covering 9fd4 (34,282) and
    2932/db1c (41,595) with ~2.4x headroom. Test parameterized on those two measured sizes.
 2. Context byte-identical: a test asserts every per-criterion call carries the assembled context
    VERBATIM, so reintroducing elision fails. Mutation-verified (truncating the context in
    _recover turns it red).
 3. criteria <= context invariant: pinned by test; mutation-verified (setting the cap back to
    24,000 turns it red).
 4. Over-cap fails fast with ZERO billable recovery calls, asserted by call count.
 5. Step-budget failure no longer blames a missing extra — PROVEN LIVE: the gate now says "The
    completion verifier ran and then failed, so this is not a missing install or credential — act
    on its own reported remedy ... Raise REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS". Genuine unavailability still gets
    the install-the-extra guidance (negative control retained).
 6. docs/llm-framework.md states the 100,000 cap, that nothing is elided, and why compaction was
    withdrawn.
 7. Landed with both votes; 1060 abandoned.

WHY COMPACTION WAS WITHDRAWN (the important part of this ticket's history). An earlier revision
compacted an over-cap context by dropping comment history oldest-first. Adversarial review proved
it a SIGNED-FALSE-PASS vector: on an epic the gate assembles one block PER TICKET
(assemble_context(graph=True)), each with its own "#### Comments" heading, so the elision silently
deleted WHOLE CHILD TICKETS — including their unmet acceptance criteria — while reporting only
that comments were removed. Reproduced directly. Elision is unsafe in BOTH directions: dropping
evidence a criterion IS met causes a false FAIL; dropping evidence it is NOT causes a false PASS.
A refusal is a visible false-block; a bad elision is an invisible signed false PASS, and this gate
SIGNS its verdict.

NOT IN SCOPE, deliberately: this does not make every large ticket verifiable. The remaining
failure modes (turn exhaustion on genuine breadth; output-token truncation into a degraded
recovery whose evidence stage is pinned at 4,096 by a min() no operator knob can lift) are
[rebar:a89d-4dd2-f421-417a], filed with all measurements.

compiled_state.description:
# Raise the completion-recovery context bound and stop misreporting the cause

Retyped from `bug` to `task`: the original report ("the close gate blames a missing `agents`
extra") was a real defect whose messaging half landed in change 1027. This ticket carries the
remaining, deliberately NARROW slice. The larger redesign — budgets that scale with criteria count
— is epic [rebar:94b4-059e-a74a-4cf8], and an advisory plan-time nudge is
[rebar:259c-0f29-e920-4fab]; neither is a prerequisite for this.

## Context / Problem

A ticket whose text merely grew large could not be closed. Bounded recovery refused any context
over 24,000 chars before doing any work, so correct, merged work had no path to `closed` except
`--force-close`. Ticket 9a08, which created this module, calls that outcome "a fail-closed
close-gate availability defect: correct, merged work cannot transition to `closed`". Reported
independently as [rebar:db1c-2a74-ffe1-4f90] on ticket 2932.

## What is PROVEN (measured, not inferred)

1. **The advertised remedy could not be carried out.** Measured on `9fd4-a94c-156e-4a56`
   (34,282 chars, reproducing its live failure byte-for-byte): description 10,281 + 9 comments
   23,617 (comments = 69%). Deleting the ENTIRE description still leaves **24,001 chars — one over
   the old limit**; comments are the only sufficient lever and the store is append-only
   (`_lib_writes` exposes `comment()` with no delete/redact). Shipped ticket 19b1 makes comments the
   sanctioned completion-evidence channel, so following the system's own guidance drove tickets
   irreversibly over the bound.
2. **The bounds were mutually incoherent.** Criteria ⊂ description ⊂ context, yet
   `_MAX_TOTAL_CRITERIA_CHARS` (32,000) > `_MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS` (24,000); a criteria set of
   26,000–31,900 chars passed every criteria bound and was then refused on context.
3. **The step-budget failure path emitted a FALSE remedy.** `transition_close.py` selected the
   remedy as `recovery_failure_cause(exc) or <install-the-extra literal>`, and
   `recovery_failure_cause` returns `None` for anything that is not a `CompletionRecoveryError`. A
   step-budget exhaustion therefore got "install the `agents` extra" after the verifier had just
   spent 804s making real model calls. Change 1027 fixed this for the recovery path only.

## Approach

Raise the context cap to **100,000 chars** and elide NOTHING. That covers both real tickets this
blocked (34,282 and 41,595) with ~2.4× headroom while still bounding the per-criterion re-send,
since recovery sends the whole context once per criterion (worst case `_MAX_CRITERIA` 32 × the
cap). Keep the cap at or above the criteria budget, pinned by an invariant test, so the incoherence
in (2) cannot return. Select the close-gate remedy by CAUSE rather than exception type, so a
failure that demonstrably ran the model stops blaming a missing dependency.

**Alternative rejected — compact an over-cap context instead of refusing it.** Implemented, then
WITHDRAWN after adversarial review proved it a signed-false-PASS vector: on an epic the gate
assembles one block per ticket (`assemble_context(graph=True)`), each with its own `#### Comments`
heading, so "drop the oldest comment history" silently deleted whole CHILD tickets — including
their unmet acceptance criteria — while reporting only that comments were removed. Reproduced
directly. Elision is unsafe in both directions: dropping evidence a criterion IS met causes a false
FAIL, dropping evidence it is NOT causes a false PASS. A refusal is a visible false-block; a bad
elision is an invisible signed false PASS, and this gate SIGNS its verdict.

**Alternative rejected — derive the cap from the model window.** `sizing.container_budget` returns
TOKENS, not characters, and `sizing.largest_window_tokens` returns the same ceiling for every model
including unknown ones, so the derivation would be both a unit error and insensitive to the
configured model. A stated constant with a recorded rationale is honest; a fake derivation is not.

**Alternative rejected — tell authors to prune tickets.** No such policy exists in this repo
predating this bug's own error string, and (1) shows pruning cannot work for a comment-dominated
ticket.

**Explicitly NOT in scope.** This does not close 9fd4: its live blocker is the primary verifier's
flat step budget, which does not scale with criteria count. That work, and the equally incoherent
evidence bounds, are epic [rebar:94b4-059e-a74a-4cf8].

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py` — raise `_MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS` to 100,000 with its
  rationale recorded; no compaction.
- `src/rebar/llm/failure.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py` — remedy selected by cause.
- `docs/llm-framework.md` §"Bounded completion recovery" — the cap, why nothing is elided, and the
  withdrawn-compaction rationale.
- `tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_recovery_oversized_d59e.py` (new),
  `tests/unit/test_close_gate_step_budget_message_d59e.py` (new). The latter does not duplicate the
  sibling `test_close_gate_bound_message_d59e.py`, which already pins the bounded-recovery remedy
  and its negative control.

## Testing

Unit tier with an injected fake runner (no billable calls). Each new test is mutation-verified by
re-introducing the exact mechanism it pins — reverting the cap, re-introducing elision, and
breaking the criteria-vs-context invariant must each turn the suite red.

Failure and edge paths: an over-cap payload must still fail fast with zero billable recovery calls;
a genuine unavailability must still receive the install-the-extra remedy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] both tickets this defect blocked — 9fd4 (34,282 chars) and 2932 (41,595 chars) — reach a
      verdict rather than a context-bound refusal, asserted by a test parameterized on those two
      measured sizes
- [ ] the context reaching the model is byte-identical to the assembled context — a test asserts
      every per-criterion call carries it verbatim, so a future reintroduction of elision fails
- [ ] `_MAX_TOTAL_CRITERIA_CHARS` can never exceed the context cap, pinned as an invariant test
- [ ] an over-cap payload still fails fast with ZERO billable recovery calls, asserted by call
      count, so raising the cap did not delete the cost guard
- [ ] a completion-verifier failure that demonstrably ran the model (a step-budget exhaustion) does
      not tell the operator to install the `agents` extra, and does surface the remedy the
      exception itself carries; a genuine unavailability STILL gets the install-the-extra guidance
- [ ] `docs/llm-framework.md` states the cap, that nothing is elided, and why compaction was
      withdrawn
- [ ] the change lands with `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`, and the superseded
      compaction revision is abandoned in Gerrit so it cannot be submitted
